steps.notes: The device key is generated by the agent and lives OUTSIDE the repo. The harness opens it only to sign the ceremony proofs (staged for replacement by an agent-side ceremony command); the command frames are signed by BACKEND custody, and the result frames only by the agent process. The root ACL is the operating system's own listing: the owner keeps FULL CONTROL and SYSTEM/Administrators are NOT excluded, while the key FILE stays owner-only (the negative control above re-adds a real foreign principal to a throwaway root and both the classifier and the real CLI refuse it).

steps.title: REGISTRATION — a real User + real JWT, then the real registration ceremony

observed.hmacLookupTagOnly: the plaintext pairing code is never persisted (accepted service law)

steps.notes: The server minted the device id and derived the device key id from the agent's own public key. The agent then adopted the server-issued id without regenerating its key.

steps.title: DATABASE TIME — the GM-44 server clock is measurable before the lease decisions

observed.eventWritten: register (real AuditEvent row, majority+j write concern, via the accepted sink)
observed.measurementIsServerTime: read with $collStats + $$NOW, so the value is the DATABASE clock

steps.notes: Without a time host the accepted services fail closed rather than deciding a lease/TTL from the writer clock, which is the correct behaviour and is why this step exists.

steps.title: PAIRING — the real ceremony through the real routes, ending in a real lease
steps.notes: Five real HTTP legs on the real router. The six-digit code is withheld from the evidence file; only its shape is recorded. The claim leg is device-authenticated (outside requireJwtAuth) and was completed with the agent's own key.

steps.title: DISPATCH — the real dispatch client signs, reserves and sends through the real relay
steps.notes: The reservation is in MongoDB before the frame reaches the wire, so a result can only be correlated to a call the platform genuinely dispatched.

steps.title: EXECUTE — the real agent verified the frame and read a real file at a real path

steps.notes: The device key lives in the agent's own store outside the repo. This harness never uses it here: a `succeeded` outcome is unreachable without a signature by that key, and only the agent process holds it while handling frames. The agent's read report and the harness's own read/write-back are separate fields on purpose: the harness's checks cannot discard the agent's proof.

steps.title: RESULT — correlated outcome: the sink completed the call the platform dispatched
steps.notes: Correlation is by the SIGNED callId against the platform's own ledger, and the ledger transitions exactly once — the durable completion write is the only one this run made.

steps.title: NEGATIVE — a frame tampered after signing must not execute and must not be a success

observed.tamperedAfterSigning: argsB64u replaced with different bytes; the signature was NOT recomputed
observed.executedMeaning: the agent refused BEFORE dispatch (ENDPOINT_ARGS_DIGEST_MISMATCH), so the tool never ran; its result payload carries only the refusal, no file content

steps.notes: The endpoint refused it (GM-47 byte-equality) before dispatch, so nothing ran and no tool output exists in its payload. The platform recorded `refused` / `success:false` and the ledger closed the call as a non-success — a completed NON-success, which is the accepted outcome law (a `refused` result is provable non-execution, not uncertainty).

steps.title: NEGATIVE — a result for an unknown callId is refused and stores nothing

observed.note: the payload is a GENUINE device-signed frame; only the call identity is wrong for it

steps.notes: The store still holds exactly the two calls that were really completed (the genuine read and the tamper refusal); the unknown call added neither a ledger row nor a stored result.

steps.title: NEGATIVE — a tool outside the server ceiling is refused before the wire

authorizeDispatch.reason: Enabled from stage B; the server ceiling is stage A. The device may only narrow the ceiling, never widen it (GM-72).

observed.gateKind: in-process call to the production module the panel route depends on

steps.notes: The gate EXISTS and is real (`deviceToolRegistry.authorizeDispatch`, the module the panel route consumes). It is NOT yet invoked by any production signing path: the accepted `relayDispatchClient` documents that wiring as the caller's job and no caller does it yet, so this refusal is genuine but not yet mechanically unavoidable from the dispatch entry point.

steps.title: AFTER — a SEPARATE process re-reads the durable ledger and cannot complete the call twice
steps.notes: This is the cross-process half of "complete exactly once": the accepted ledger's own conditional completion, backed by this harness's compare-and-set store.

steps.title: FINAL LEDGER — the platform's own durable record of every call in this run
steps.notes: Two calls: the genuine read (completed/succeeded) and the tampered frame (completed/refused). Nothing else.

steps.title: CLEANUP — the harness database is dropped and no harness-prefixed database remains

observed.note: no other database appeared during this run

limits.statement: The server tool-policy gate is real but not yet wired into the production dispatch path: `deviceToolRegistry.assertDispatchAllowed` exists and refuses correctly, while `relayDispatchClient.dispatchCommand` does not call it. This harness therefore proves the gate's own behaviour (in-process, against the production module) and NOT that every production dispatch is gated.
